physicalNotes: Radius 0.1390849 Jupiter radii from Egger et al. 2025 (2025A&A...696A..28E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...696A..28E/abstract): 9,943.5 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.01060321 Jupiter masses (Egger et al. 2025, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2025A&A...696A..28E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...696A..28E/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Egger et al. 2025 (2025A&A...696A..28E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EGGER_ET_AL__2025): P 1.273099 d
sources.shape: Egger et al. 2025 (2025A&A...696A..28E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EGGER_ET_AL__2025): a/R* 6.03; Suárez Mascareño et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..56S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname SUAREZ_MASCARENO_ET_AL_2024): inclination 84.6 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Egger et al. 2025 (2025A&A...696A..28E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EGGER_ET_AL__2025): transit mid-time 2460205.7524 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 2 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
